findings.failure_mode: missing or unreadable config/shard file aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, ShardError> and use map_err(|e| ShardError::Io(e))

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on invalid numeric input
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV line aborts the program instead of returning a typed Parse/Invalid error
findings.fix: use map_err(|_| ShardError::Parse) and propagate Result through the parser

findings.problem: as u16 casts a u32 value without bounds checking
findings.failure_mode: values > 65535 silently truncate to 16-bit, producing incorrect records with no error signal
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| ShardError::Overflow) or parse directly as u16

findings.problem: parts[0] uses unchecked indexing on a user-supplied line split
findings.failure_mode: empty or comma-less lines panic with index-out-of-bounds
findings.fix: use parts.get(0).ok_or(...) or split_once(',') and handle the missing field with a typed error

findings.problem: parts[1] uses unchecked indexing on a user-supplied line split
findings.failure_mode: lines with only one field panic with index-out-of-bounds
findings.fix: use parts.get(1).ok_or(...) or split_once(',') and handle the missing field with a typed error

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", ...) is an I/O side effect embedded in the parsing loop
findings.failure_mode: pure parsing logic is contaminated with logging, making the core non-deterministic and untestable
findings.fix: move all I/O (file reads, logging, printing) to a shell layer; the core parser should accept &str and return pure Records

findings.problem: Record uses raw String and u16 primitives instead of typed domain newtypes
findings.failure_mode: no compile-time enforcement of name rules (e.g. non-empty, valid characters) or value ranges (0..=65535)
findings.fix: introduce a Name(String) newtype with a fallible constructor and use it in Record; parse at the boundary

findings.problem: load_shards returns Vec<Record> with no error type, using panic as error handling
findings.failure_mode: all failure modes (I/O, parse, overflow, missing fields, empty lines) are collapsed into panics with no recovery path
findings.fix: define a ShardError enum (Io, Parse, EmptyLine, MissingField, Overflow, Allocation) and return Result<Vec<Record>, ShardError>

findings.problem: Vec<String> collected from line.split(',') with no capacity hint or upper bound
findings.failure_mode: a single line with thousands of commas allocates unboundedly, enabling memory exhaustion from a single input line
findings.fix: use split_once(',') instead of splitting all parts, or pre-allocate with a known small max and enforce it

findings.problem: load_shards couples I/O (fs::read_to_string) with parsing logic in a single function
findings.failure_mode: cannot test the parsing logic in isolation; the pure core is not extractable
findings.fix: split into a pure parse_records(&[str]) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> and a shell function load_shards(path) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ShardError> that reads the file and delegates

findings.problem: no [dev-dependencies] for criterion or other benchmark framework; no benchmarks/ directory
findings.failure_mode: no performance baseline or regression guard for shard loading throughput or memory usage
findings.fix: add criterion as dev-dependency and write a microbenchmark for parse_records with representative shard data

findings.problem: no allocation profiling evidence; function allocates Vec, Strings per line, and per-part copies with zero-copy avoidance
findings.failure_mode: unknown heap pressure; a production path through this function may exceed memory budgets under load
findings.fix: add allocation profiling (e.g. dhat, or jemalloc profiler) and benchmark; consider parsing in-place with &str instead of cloning Strings

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for shard-loading throughput or allocation profile
no profiler data (dhat/criterion-03) for memory allocation patterns
no second-ring verification (Kani bounded model check for index bounds and overflow paths)
no command evidence that cargo fmt, cargo clippy, or cargo test pass
no allocation budget or maximum-line-width contract documented
residual_risk: Static review only with no commands run. All five unwrap/panic paths, two unchecked indexing paths, the lossy as-u16 cast, hidden println I/O in core, absence of typed errors, unbounded Vec allocation per line, and missing benchmark/profiler/evidence are BLOCKER-severity issues that must be fixed before delivery. The code as written will panic on any malformed input, missing file, or out-of-range value, and has no performance or allocation guarantees.
